answer: Arrival-tide gating.** New agent identities activate only after their inbound request timing matches the platform's historical daily tide of organic joins; a lone clone arriving off-peak stays inert. Each identity must then hold a unique traffic haven—a reserved slot with its own burst budget—so mass signups fragment into visible clusters. Registration costs an attacker one isolated IP block and a sustained request orchard warm-up of roughly two weeks per identity before any call executes. Cloning at scale forfeits the timing camouflage that makes activation cheap.
